description: A 40-case evaluation corpus of realistic MSP helpdesk tickets labeled under KB-006. OpenAI Codex authored the cases to cover incidents, misleading reassurances, routine work, and incident-shaped benign requests.

provenance.author: OpenAI Codex (GPT-5), 2026-07-29
materials_withheld: The held-out detection implementation, its prompts or rules beyond KB-006, prior evaluation cases, and evaluation results
provenance.isolation: Work was performed in the supplied project directory, and reads were limited to the four named files in that directory; no web access or material outside the directory was used.
provenance.known_leakage: The commissioning brief supplied seam-specific directions for hard_negative cases: admitted self-lockouts, user-caused file loss, independently verified payment changes, slow non-message items, genuine vendor SSO redirects, mechanically caused odd behavior, and safely ignored phishing. This guidance applies only to hard_negative cases; no comparable scenario guidance was supplied for incident cases, so the recall figure is unaffected. Outside-list incidents were written from general security knowledge, not from prior knowledge of this project or its held-out detector.

cases.subject: w2 page went blank
cases.body: I got an email saying my W-2 was ready and used the blue button. It looked like our Microsoft screen, so I put in my work email, password, and the code from my phone, then the page went blank.
cases.rationale: The user submitted authentication information and an MFA code through an untrusted email flow, indicating active account compromise.

cases.subject: invoice made laptop noisy
cases.body: Sorry, I opened the Word invoice from a trucking company and pressed Enable Content because it was empty. Since then a black window blinks on and off every few minutes and the fan will not settle down.
cases.rationale: An unanticipated document was opened and immediately followed by new system behavior.

cases.subject: documents have dot luna
cases.body: Nobody can open the estimating folder; every filename ends in .luna now, and a new desktop text file demands bitcoin before Friday.
cases.rationale: The inaccessible altered files and payment demand show an active extortion event.

cases.subject: browser will not leave alert
cases.body: Chrome keeps launching by itself to a red page that says call support, even after I close it. Also my usual start page has been replaced with a search site I have never used.
cases.rationale: The unsolicited browser launches, scare page, and replaced start page are direct takeover symptoms.

cases.subject: fwd customer question
cases.body: Forwarded message: "Why are you sending me document links at 2 in the morning from melissa@northstarfab.com?" I am Melissa and I did not send these, and there is nothing like them in my Sent folder.
cases.rationale: A customer received messages presented as coming from the client's domain that the named sender did not originate.

cases.subject: supplier wants new routing
cases.body: Brightline Parts says today's $38,400 invoice has to go to a different account. Their old bank is supposedly frozen. They want it done before noon, and this is not how they usually contact me.
cases.rationale: An unusual vendor message urgently redirects a substantial payment to new banking coordinates.

cases.subject: locked out during lunch
cases.body: Phone note: Dana returned from lunch to find her account disabled after repeated tries, although her laptop was shut in her desk and she had not tried to sign in anywhere today.
cases.rationale: The lockout was generated by login attempts the user states she did not make.

cases.subject: phone kept asking approve
cases.body: My phone asked me to approve a work sign-in about eight times while I was driving. I tapped yes once just to stop it, but I was not trying to log in.
cases.rationale: The user approved an authentication request they did not initiate, creating a clear unauthorized-access risk.

cases.subject: laptop bag missing
cases.body: My work laptop was taken from my car at the clinic parking lot about twenty minutes ago. It was asleep, still signed in, and the patient scheduling program was open when I closed the lid.
cases.rationale: A stolen signed-in device exposes active access to company and patient systems.

cases.subject: mouse moving on its own
cases.body: With my hands off the mouse, I watched the pointer open our payroll folder and start copying employee spreadsheets into a zip file while nobody else was in the office.
cases.rationale: Observed remote control is actively accessing and packaging sensitive payroll data without authorization.

cases.subject: please pull back my email
cases.body: I messed up. Autocomplete sent the salary spreadsheet to karen@gmail.com instead of Karen here. It includes names, home addresses, and tax ID numbers.
cases.rationale: Sensitive employee data was disclosed to an unintended external recipient.

cases.subject: who is temp-admin
cases.body: There is a new user called temp-admin under Other users on the shipping PC, created at 2:14 this morning. I checked with both supervisors and neither of them made it.
cases.rationale: An unapproved local account with an administrative name appeared outside working hours.

cases.subject: usb does nothing
cases.body: Found a thumb drive by our loading dock and put it in the receiving computer. A little black box flashed. The drive looks empty, and now the computer is sending print jobs I did not request.
cases.rationale: An unknown found device was connected and immediately triggered unexplained execution and system actions.

cases.subject: how did eric reply
cases.body: Eric left two weeks ago, yet his work mailbox replied in our shared sales thread this morning even though HR says nobody was authorized to use it.
cases.rationale: A departed employee's mailbox is being used after access should have ended and no replacement user was authorized.

cases.subject: folder link was set wrong
cases.body: I just noticed the board folder link was set to anyone on the internet, not our directors. The activity page shows an outside address downloaded all 23 files yesterday.
cases.rationale: Confidential board files were publicly exposed and demonstrably downloaded by an unknown external party.

cases.subject: need regular password reset
cases.body: I used the HR email button and typed my login into the page, but it said invalid. A caller claiming to be our IT partner said he reviewed it, called it a normal sync problem, and told support to only reset my password.
cases.rationale: The claimed reassurance does not change that the user gave login information to an unverified page reached through email.

cases.subject: approved test software
cases.body: A caller had me install QuickAssist Plus and read the connection number. They are moving around in our invoicing program now, but their chat calls it an authorized quarterly test and says support must not interrupt.
cases.rationale: An unverified caller obtained live remote control of a financial application, regardless of the authorization claim in their chat.

cases.subject: update stuck shared drive
cases.body: All the shop drawings now end in .k2, and a note wants payment for the key. The software vendor emailed that IT already cleared this as a display issue and says not to escalate.
cases.rationale: The file changes and extortion note are an active incident even though an embedded reassurance calls them a display issue.

cases.subject: login drill completed
cases.body: A helpdesk caller knew my name and asked me to read the six-digit code that appeared, which I did. He called it an approved internal drill and said no report should be opened.
cases.rationale: An unsolicited caller obtained a live authentication code, and their assertion of approval is not evidence of authorization.

cases.subject: popup already cleared
cases.body: Edge keeps opening to a full-screen warning with a number to call. A voicemail claiming to be Summit's monitoring desk calls it a known false alarm and says to skip the usual process.
cases.rationale: Recurring unsolicited scare pages are incident symptoms, and an unverified voicemail cannot clear them.

cases.subject: printer refuses checks
cases.body: This printer is driving me nuts: it says LOAD TRAY 2 for checks, plain paper from tray 1 works, and the smaller check stock is gone.
cases.rationale: The explicit media-tray condition is routine printer maintenance, not suspicious machine behavior.

cases.subject: cad says no seats
cases.body: Tom's CAD says all licenses are in use. The message lists the six designer workstations that currently have a seat, and I checked that all six people are working. We added Tom yesterday but purchasing only bought six seats for seven designers, so can you add one?
cases.rationale: A known license-seat shortage explains the message and does not resemble malicious software activity beyond a generic application failure.

cases.subject: working home friday
cases.body: Working from home Friday for the first time, please put the company VPN on my assigned laptop and show me where to sign in.
cases.rationale: This is a prospective access setup request, not evidence of unauthorized access or stolen authentication information.

cases.subject: new girl starts monday
cases.body: Please create email and scheduling access for Priya N. starting Monday. She is replacing Alice at reception and will use the front desk computer. Her manager completed the HR form, including the access list and start date, and approved it below.
cases.rationale: A manager-approved new-hire setup is ordinary onboarding, not the appearance of an unauthorized account.

cases.subject: server down at 8?
cases.body: Just checking that the file server will be unavailable at 8 tonight as announced so night shift knows whether to finish labels first.
cases.rationale: The anticipated interruption matches announced maintenance rather than an unexplained or hostile outage.

cases.subject: old phone in emails
cases.body: Forwarded from office manager: "Our main number changes to 555-0148 on August 1; please update my Outlook footer to match."
cases.rationale: The user is requesting an intentional signature edit, not reporting mail sent under a false identity.

cases.subject: password expires tomorrow
cases.body: Windows says my password expires tomorrow, which matches the reminder I have been seeing all week. I have not changed it yet. Can you send the normal steps before I leave for vacation, or call me after the 2 p.m. staff meeting?
cases.rationale: An expected expiry reminder with no unrecognized activity is routine password maintenance, not an unauthorized account change.

cases.subject: screen blink
cases.body: Second monitor goes black for a second if I bump the desk. I pushed the loose HDMI plug back in and it returns, but it will not stay tight.
cases.rationale: A loose display cable fully explains the repeatable flicker, rather than remote screen control or malware.

cases.subject: add lee to orders
cases.body: Maria is out for surgery, so her manager asked that Lee get access to the orders mailbox through next month. Lee already handles the same orders when Maria is at lunch. The manager's request, dates, and approval are all in the forwarded thread below.
cases.rationale: Documented temporary mailbox access is an authorized permission change, not account compromise.

cases.subject: scanners slow at lunch
cases.body: All four warehouse scanners lag around noon when everyone is in the break room streaming video. The wired packing computer stays normal, and the scanners recover when lunch ends. We have seen the same pattern every weekday this month; can we get better wireless coverage?
cases.rationale: A repeatable congestion pattern tied to known network use is a capacity issue, not malicious system behavior.

cases.subject: i locked myself out
cases.body: My fault: Caps Lock was on and I kept trying the same password until the account locked, so please unlock me.
cases.rationale: The user identifies the repeated attempts that caused the lockout, unlike an unexplained lockout caused by someone else.

cases.subject: restore archive please
cases.body: Sorry, this was me. I deleted the 2023 Jobs folder while cleaning the shared drive, then emptied the recycle bin before I noticed. Can yesterday's copy be restored?
cases.rationale: The requester explicitly caused an ordinary deletion, which can resemble malicious file loss but has a complete mundane explanation.

cases.subject: update oak street bank info
cases.body: Oak Street Medical moved banks and sent new ACH instructions. I called Jenna at the number already saved in our vendor master. She confirmed the exact numbers, and our controller signed the change form.
cases.rationale: The vendor change was independently confirmed through a previously known channel and internally approved, so it is not the fraudulent-payment pattern it resembles.

cases.subject: report takes forever
cases.body: The quarterly inventory report takes about four minutes to open from the reporting program. It is 600 pages and does open eventually; emails and downloaded documents are fine.
cases.rationale: A very large known report is merely slow to render, which is not the opened-message or attachment sequence associated with an incident.

cases.subject: payroll login looks different
cases.body: Payroll bookmark send us to new blue sign-in screen. I phoned vendor using support number in our contract. They confirm this morning all customers now use that exact address.
cases.rationale: The unfamiliar redirect was verified with the vendor through a preexisting contact method, distinguishing it from credential capture.

cases.subject: cursor keeps pulling left
cases.body: Karen next to me says her pointer keeps sliding left. I turned the mouse over and a shipping label is stuck across the sensor; it stops when the label is removed, but we need a replacement because the glue will not come off.
cases.rationale: A visible obstruction produces and stops the cursor movement, ruling out the remote-control incident it superficially resembles.

cases.subject: junk voicemail email
cases.body: Got a strange 'new voicemail' email from outside. I did not press anything. I did not open the included file, reply, or type information anywhere. It is deleted; do you want the sender address?
cases.rationale: The suspicious message was recognized and ignored with no interaction, so the triggering actions for a phishing or attachment incident did not occur.

cases.subject: yes that password email was me
cases.body: I changed my password from the office at 9:12 and received the confirmation right afterward. I am confirming it was me because the notice said to contact support if it was not.
cases.rationale: The user knowingly performed the password change at the matching time, unlike an unrecognized change notification.

cases.subject: undo my file names
cases.body: This is embarrassing. I pressed Run on the bulk rename tool and watched it put FINAL_ in front of all 412 product photos. They still open; can you undo my batch?
cases.rationale: The user directly initiated a cosmetic batch rename and the files remain usable, unlike hostile alteration or encryption.

cases.subject: put old start page back
cases.body: I changed Edge's start page to weather yesterday. I do not like it. Please put our intranet back; nothing opens unless I start the browser myself.
cases.rationale: The requester intentionally changed the browser setting and reports no unsolicited launches, unlike browser takeover symptoms.
